new.title: One adaptive phase query after d fixed determinant queries recovers every complex matching product
new.statement:
∀ (n q : ℕ) (H : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (ζ : ℂ), 0 < n → IsPrimitiveRoot ζ q →
  let I := Fin n
  let E := I × I
  let V := Submodule.span ℚ {v : E → ℚ | ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm I, (∀ j, H (σ j) j = true) ∧
    v = fun e => if σ e.2 = e.1 then (1 : ℚ) else 0}
  let d := Module.finrank ℚ V
  let W := Equiv.Perm I → ℂ
  let S := E → Fin q
  let fits := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) => ∀ i j, H i j = false → A i j = 0
  let w := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) (π : Equiv.Perm I) => ∏ j : I, A (π j) j
  let eval := fun (s : S) (A : Matrix I I ℂ) =>
    Matrix.det (fun i j => A i j * ζ ^ (s (i,j)).val : Matrix I I ℂ)
  n * (n ^ d) ^ 2 < q →
  ∃ (front : Fin d → S) (last : (Fin d → ℂ) → S) (read : (Fin d → ℂ) → ℂ → W),
    ∀ A : Matrix I I ℂ, fits A →
      let y := fun h : Fin d => eval (front h) A
      read y (eval (last y) A) = w A
new.unlocks: Identifies every matching product from rank-many fixed determinant replies and a single final phase evaluation chosen from those replies.
new.context: Use the bounded list for the d replies. Two distinct candidate vectors give a nonzero signed difference polynomial in the entry phases: different permutations use different monomials of degree n. On the qth-root grid each pair collides on at most n/q of the points. Sum over at most choose(n^d,2) pairs and fix a phase pattern avoiding them all for that list. Read the unique candidate giving the final answer. Empty lists need only a default decoder.

new.title: For b disjoint two-by-two blocks the exact adaptive determinant query count is b+2
new.statement:
∀ blockCount : ℕ, 2 ≤ blockCount →
  let I := Fin blockCount × Fin 2
  let E := I × I
  let S := E → ℂ
  let W := Equiv.Perm I → ℂ
  let fits := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) => ∀ i j : I, i.1 ≠ j.1 → A i j = 0
  let w := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) (π : Equiv.Perm I) => ∏ j : I, A (π j) j
  let eval := fun (s : S) (A : Matrix I I ℂ) =>
    Matrix.det (fun i j => A i j * s (i,j) : Matrix I I ℂ)
  (∀ ask : ℕ → List ℂ → S,
    let run := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) => (List.range (blockCount+1)).foldl
      (fun h j => eval (ask j h) A :: h) ([] : List ℂ)
    ∃ A B : Matrix I I ℂ, fits A ∧ fits B ∧ run A = run B ∧ w A ≠ w B) ∧
  ∀ (q : ℕ) (ζ : ℂ), blockCount < q → blockCount * Nat.choose blockCount.factorial 2 < q → IsPrimitiveRoot ζ q →
    let T := E → Fin q
    let phase := fun (t : T) (e : E) => ζ ^ (t e).val
    ∃ (front : Fin (blockCount+1) → T) (last : (Fin (blockCount+1) → ℂ) → T) (read : (Fin (blockCount+1) → ℂ) → ℂ → W),
      ∀ A : Matrix I I ℂ, fits A →
        let y := fun h : Fin (blockCount+1) => eval (phase (front h)) A
        read y (eval (phase (last y)) A) = w A
new.unlocks: Gives the exact deterministic adaptive query count for every number of disjoint two-by-two complex blocks, even against arbitrary complex multipliers in the lower bound.
new.context: Write the matching tensor as a product of b two-vectors. Along b zero replies, assign a distinct block kernel to each test. Interchanging assignments gives two tensor lines if any block has unequal kernels. Otherwise one block kills every test and another varies. Scale on these lines to defeat the last linear test. For the upper bound interpolate the product of b binary linear forms at b+1 common phases. Factorization leaves at most b! ordered tensors, including factors at infinity. An independent phase in each block distinguishes the list by the grid bound.

new.title: Rank-many phase determinant queries leave at most n^d possible matching-product vectors
new.statement:
∀ (n q : ℕ) (H : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (ζ : ℂ), 0 < n → IsPrimitiveRoot ζ q →
  let I := Fin n
  let E := I × I
  let V := Submodule.span ℚ {v : E → ℚ | ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm I, (∀ j, H (σ j) j = true) ∧
    v = fun e => if σ e.2 = e.1 then (1 : ℚ) else 0}
  let d := Module.finrank ℚ V
  let W := Equiv.Perm I → ℂ
  let S := E → Fin q
  let fits := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) => ∀ i j, H i j = false → A i j = 0
  let w := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) (π : Equiv.Perm I) => ∏ j : I, A (π j) j
  let eval := fun (s : S) (A : Matrix I I ℂ) =>
    Matrix.det (fun i j => A i j * ζ ^ (s (i,j)).val : Matrix I I ℂ)
  n * n ^ d < q →
  ∃ (front : Fin d → S) (candidates : (Fin d → ℂ) → Finset W),
    (∀ y, (candidates y).card ≤ n ^ d) ∧
    ∀ A : Matrix I I ℂ, fits A → w A ∈ candidates (fun h => eval (front h) A)
new.unlocks: Bounds the number of candidate matching vectors after rank-many phase queries, including inputs on the coordinate boundary.
new.context: Choose d edge coordinates spanning the dual of the exponent span. Their monomial chart parametrizes the dense image torus by solving logarithmic linear equations. Pull back a generic linear section and apply Bezout to bound its degree by D=n^d. At each projective cut avoid one point per component: each point gives a nonzero determinant polynomial of degree n on the phase grid. The union bound costs nD/q. After d cuts the common kernel misses the projective image. Each affine fiber is finite of size at most D by homogenizing its linear equations.

changed.title: Find a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit for cyclic count parity on 4 sites and window 2 with at most 20 AND/OR gates
changed.statement:
let n := 4
let w := 1
let P := 2^(w+1)
let inv := fun (G : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (G.gates.filter (fun g => @decide (g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) (Classical.propDecidable _))).length
let binary := fun (G : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) => G.size - inv G
let loc := fun k : Nat => (⟨k % n, Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.succ_pos 3)⟩ : Fin n)
let fits := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ ∀ raw : Fin (n*P) → Bool,
    let entries := List.ofFn raw
    let pass := fun (x : Fin n → Bool) => ∀ i : Fin n,
      let word := ∑ j : Fin (w+1), if x (loc (i.val+j.val)) then 2^j.val else 0
      entries.getD (i.val*P+word) false = true
    C.eval entries = (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Bool)).filter pass).card).testBit 0
∃ C, fits C ∧ binary C ≤ 20
changed.unlocks: a smaller circuit here refutes the gate floor L-clb-120 at n=4, window 2
changed.context: A find is one explicit gate list on the 16 raw entries, checked by decide over all 2^16 tables (NOT gates free, AND/OR at most 20). L-clb-120 prices this case at 21 AND/OR gates: restrict to single entries per row to see each usable entry must be read, then count the forced binary gates. Search below that count; a hit refutes the floor of L-clb-120 at n=4, and a hand-back saying the floor stands is useful data.

changed.title: All independent binary-clause edits around one fixed word split into disjoint chains and squares
changed.statement:
let W := fun n : ℕ => Fin n → Bool
let F := fun n : ℕ => Finset ((Fin n × Bool) × (Fin n × Bool))
let sat := fun (n : ℕ) (A : F n) (x : W n) =>
  ∀ c ∈ A, x c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ x c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2
let delta := fun (n : ℕ) (r z : W n) =>
  Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => z i ≠ r i)
let free := fun (n : ℕ) (r : W n) (S : Finset (W n)) =>
  ∀ D : Finset (W n), D ⊆ S → ∃ A : F n, ∀ x : W n,
    (sat n A x ↔ (x = r ∨ x ∈ D))
∀ (n : ℕ) (r : W n) (S : Finset (W n)), r ∉ S →
  let T := S.image (delta n r)
  let tops := T.filter (fun U => ∀ V ∈ T, U ⊆ V → U = V)
  (free n r S ↔
    ((∀ U ∈ tops, ∀ V ∈ tops, U ≠ V → Disjoint U V) ∧
     ∀ U ∈ tops,
       ((∀ X ∈ T, X ⊆ U → ∀ Y ∈ T, Y ⊆ U → X ⊆ Y ∨ Y ⊆ X) ∨
        (∃ X ∈ T, ∃ Y ∈ T, X.Nonempty ∧ Y.Nonempty ∧ Disjoint X Y ∧
          X ∪ Y = U ∧ ∀ Z ∈ T, Z ⊆ U → (Z = X ∨ Z = Y ∨ Z = U)))))
changed.unlocks: Classifies exactly which truth-table bits can be independently edited above a single fixed passing word.
changed.context: Translate the root to zero. With two switches their intersection is the majority with zero, forcing incomparable supports to be disjoint. For incomparable X,Y below a maximum U, their majority with U forces U to be their union. Any nonempty proper subset of X would force a different union with Y and U. A support meeting both contains both. Conversely every subfamily with zero is stable under majority within chains and squares. Two local supports with an outside point intersect in a selected member or zero. Reconstruct by pair projections.

changed.title: One fixed word permits exactly n plus half of n rounded down independent binary-clause switches, with all maximizers given by matchings
changed.statement:
let W := fun n : ℕ => Fin n → Bool
let F := fun n : ℕ => Finset ((Fin n × Bool) × (Fin n × Bool))
let sat := fun (n : ℕ) (A : F n) (x : W n) =>
  ∀ c ∈ A, x c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ x c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2
let delta := fun (n : ℕ) (r z : W n) =>
  Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => z i ≠ r i)
let free := fun (n : ℕ) (r : W n) (S : Finset (W n)) =>
  ∀ D : Finset (W n), D ⊆ S → ∃ A : F n, ∀ x : W n,
    (sat n A x ↔ (x = r ∨ x ∈ D))
∀ (n : ℕ) (r : W n),
  (∃ S : Finset (W n), r ∉ S ∧ free n r S ∧ S.card = n + n / 2) ∧
  ∀ S : Finset (W n), r ∉ S → free n r S →
    S.card ≤ n + n / 2 ∧
    (S.card = n + n / 2 ↔
      ∃ P : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), P.card = n / 2 ∧
        (∀ e ∈ P, e.card = 2) ∧
        (∀ e ∈ P, ∀ f ∈ P, e ≠ f → Disjoint e f) ∧
        ∀ z : W n, (z ∈ S ↔ ((delta n r z).card = 1 ∨ delta n r z ∈ P)))
changed.unlocks: Determines the full switch capacity over a single permanent solution and identifies every family attaining the bound.
changed.context: Count k square blocks. Each contributes three switches on two or more coordinates. A nested block contributes at most its number of coordinates since strict inclusions use fresh coordinates. Thus s is at most n+k and k is at most floor(n/2). Equality forces k disjoint two-coordinate squares with at most one coordinate left, accounted for by a singleton. Conversely use the one-coordinate flips and the paired double flips. The disjoint block criterion permits every subset, including at arity zero.

changed.title: The number of fixed passing words bounds independent binary-clause switches by twice the arity plus a quadratic in the fixed count
changed.statement:
let W := fun n : ℕ => Fin n → Bool
let F := fun n : ℕ => Finset ((Fin n × Bool) × (Fin n × Bool))
let sat := fun (n : ℕ) (A : F n) (x : W n) =>
  ∀ c ∈ A, x c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ x c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2
let free := fun (n : ℕ) (B S : Finset (W n)) =>
  Disjoint B S ∧ ∀ D : Finset (W n), D ⊆ S → ∃ A : F n,
    ∀ x : W n, (sat n A x ↔ (x ∈ B ∨ x ∈ D))
∀ n : ℕ,
  (∀ B S : Finset (W n), free n B S →
    S.card ≤ 2 * n + 1 + B.card * B.card / 4) ∧
  ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → m ≤ n →
    ∃ B S : Finset (W n), free n B S ∧ B.card = m + 1 ∧
      S.card = m * m / 4 + 2 * (n - m)
changed.unlocks: Bounds independent answers by the number of permanently passing words, with a construction whose gap is independent of the ambient arity.
changed.context: Remove a side with at most two passing words by fixing its opposite. Otherwise write each support as a union of principal supports above a passing root. A switch has at most two maximal classes. With two it is terminal. A switch neighbor after one drop would force the surviving bit to occur in just that neighbor and its top. Both lower neighbors are therefore fixed. Their pairs are triangle-free since the majority on a triangle contains all three distinct terminal words. Append two selectable points above adjacent fixed words per extra bit in the balanced-block construction.

changed.title: Exactly the individual mixed sites maximize one-query whole-word prediction on large singular spacing-two banks
changed.statement:
∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t), 240 ≤ t →
  letI : ∀ p : Prop, Decidable p := Classical.propDecidable
  let F := ZMod 2
  let n := 6*t
  let W := Fin n → F
  let ix := fun j : ℕ => (⟨j % n, Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.zero_lt_succ 5) ht)⟩ : Fin n)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : W) (i : Fin n) => w (ix (i.val + n - s % n))
  let out := fun (name c raw : W) (i : Fin n) =>
    let old := rot 3 raw + name
    let y := fun j : Fin n => old j + old (ix (j.val+2)) + old (ix (j.val+n-2))
    y i + (1+y (ix (i.val+1)))*y (ix (i.val+2)) + rot 4 raw i + c i
  let mix := fun (w : W) (i : Fin n) =>
    let old := rot 3 w
    old i + old (ix (i.val+2)) + old (ix (i.val+n-2))
  ∀ name c : W,
    let hits := fun (q : W →ₗ[F] F) (A : F → W →ₗ[F] W) (b : F → W) =>
      Nat.card {w : W // out name c w = A (q w) w + b (q w)}
    ∀ q : W →ₗ[F] F,
      (∃ A b, ∀ (q' : W →ₗ[F] F) A' b', hits q' A' b' ≤ hits q A b) ↔
        ∃ i : Fin n, ∀ w : W, q w = mix w i

A mixed query can double a scalar bias only if both slopes lie in the respective images of the bilinear matrix. If both are site evaluations, select one edge incident at the left site and missing the right site. This character makes the mixed query strictly worse. changed.title: Counting distinct one-hot tables at each weighted parity error under a one-layer nonlinear gate budget
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
    xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
        (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (Q : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (Q.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun h => ds.getD h 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD Q.output 0
∀ (a b m t : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let M := Matrix (Fin (a+1)) (Fin (b+1)) F
  let T := Fin (a+1) → Fin (b+1) → Bool
  ∀ (B : Fin m → M) (value : Fin m → F) (w : Fin m → ℕ),
  let gauss := fun (u d : ℕ) =>
    (Nat.card {W : Submodule F (Fin u → F) // Module.finrank F W = d} : ℤ)
  let shell := fun (j h : ℕ) =>
    ∑ d ∈ Finset.range (j+1), (-1 : ℤ)^(j-d) * 2^(Nat.choose (j-d) 2) *
      2^(b*d) * gauss (a-h) d * gauss (a-d) (j-d)
  let test := fun (P : T) (i : Fin m) =>
    ∑ x, ∑ y, B i x y * (if P x y then (1 : F) else 0)
  let loss := fun (P : T) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => test P i ≠ value i)).sum w
  let realizable := fun (P : T) => ∃ Q : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    (∀ g ∈ Q.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (a+1+(b+1)) Q ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents P Q ∧
    depth (a+1+(b+1)) Q ≤ 1 ∧ Q.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t
  let X : Polynomial ℤ := Polynomial.X
  let mass := ∑ P : T, @ite (Polynomial ℤ) (realizable P) (Classical.propDecidable _)
    (X ^ loss P) 0
  let weight := fun (S : Finset (Fin m)) =>
    let D := S.sum B
    let even := (∀ x, (∑ y, D x y) = 0) ∧ (∀ y, (∑ x, D x y) = 0)
    let h := Matrix.rank (D.submatrix Fin.succ Fin.succ)
    if even then
      (if S.sum value = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1) * 2^(a+b+1) *
        (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (min a (2*t)+1), shell j h)
    else 0
  Polynomial.C ((2 : ℤ)^m) * mass =
    ∑ S : Finset (Fin m), Polynomial.C (weight S) *
      (∏ i ∈ S, (1-X^(w i))) * (∏ i ∈ Finset.univ \ S, (1+X^(w i)))

Each surviving offset sum contributes 2^(a+b+1). Sum over answer words with their loss monomials. Each test gives 1-X^w inside the subset and 1+X^w outside.

changed.title: Encoder gate budgets determine pointwise equality-parity savings in each open bias interval and at the first endpoint
changed.statement:
∀ (a r : Nat), 3 ≤ a → 0 < r →
  let q := 2^a
  let ρ : ℚ := 1 - 4 / (q : ℚ)
  let τ := fun (j : Nat) => ρ^j / (1+ρ^j)
  ∀ β : ℚ, τ (r+1) < β → (β < τ r ∨ (r = 1 ∧ β = τ r)) →
    ∃ K : Nat, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (m g : Nat), 0 < m →
      let n := a*m
      let W := Fin m → Fin a → Bool
      let Circ := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit
      let legal := fun (C : Circ) =>
        (∀ i : Fin C.gates.length, ∀ v ∈ (C.gates.get i).inputs, v < n+i.val) ∧
        (∀ h ∈ C.gates, h.inputs.length ≤ 2 ∧
          (h.op = .and ∨ h.op = .or ∨ h.op = .mod 2 ∨ (h.op = .not ∧ h.inputs.length = 1)))
      let cost := fun (C : Circ) => C.gates.countP (fun h => @decide
        ((h.op = .and ∨ h.op = .or) ∧ h.inputs.length = 2) (Classical.propDecidable _))
      let works := fun (b : Nat) =>
        b ≤ n ∧ ∃ (z : Nat) (C : Fin z → Circ) (tap : Fin z → Fin (n-b) → Nat)
          (read : Fin z → (Fin (n-b) → Bool) → W → Bool),
          0 < z ∧ (∀ s, legal (C s) ∧ cost (C s) ≤ g ∧
            ∀ j, tap s j < n+(C s).gates.length) ∧
          ∀ x y : W,
            let truth := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).filter (fun i => x i = y i)).card % 2 == 1
            let hits := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin z)).filter (fun s =>
              read s (fun j => ((C s).wires ((List.ofFn x).flatMap (fun v => List.ofFn v))).getD
                (tap s j) false) y = truth)).card
            (1+β)*(z : ℚ) ≤ 2*(hits : ℚ)
      let scale := (1+min m g)^r
      (∀ b : Nat, works b → 2^b ≤ K*scale) ∧
        ∃ b : Nat, works b ∧ scale ≤ K*2^b

changed.title: One red-blue graph preserves every size and signed-score count of optimal fan-in-two AND/OR equality functions, with a converse for Exact Matching
changed.statement:
let header := fun j : Nat => List.replicate j true ++ [false]
let fast := fun f : List Bool → List Bool =>
  ∃ M : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => x) (fun x : List Bool => x) f,
    ∀ i, Finite (M.tm.Γ i)
let bits := fun (w z : Nat) => (List.range w).map (fun h => z.testBit h)
let pairs := fun k : Nat => (List.finRange k).flatMap (fun i =>
    ((List.finRange k).filter (fun j => decide (i < j))).map (fun j => (i,j)))
let paint := fun (k : Nat) (G R : Fin k → Fin k → Bool) =>
  header k ++ (pairs k).flatMap (fun z => [G z.1 z.2, R z.1 z.2])
let perfect := fun (k : Nat) (G : Fin k → Fin k → Bool) (P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) =>
  Function.Involutive P ∧ ∀ i, P i ≠ i ∧ G (min i (P i)) (max i (P i)) = true
∃ write decode reverseQ : List Bool → List Bool, fast write ∧ fast decode ∧ fast reverseQ ∧
  (
∀ (n : Nat), 2 ≤ n →
  ∀ (hard : List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)))
    (soft : List ((Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)) × Bool)),
  let m := soft.length
  let ends := fun e : Fin n × Fin n => ({e.1,e.2} : Finset (Fin n))
  let E := (pairs n).toFinset.filter (fun e =>
    ∀ z ∈ hard, ¬(ends e ⊆ z.1) ∧ ¬(ends e ⊆ z.2))
  let lists := fun (S : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) (t : (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)) × Bool) =>
    Disjoint t.1.1 t.1.2 ∧ ∀ e ∈ S, ends e ⊆ t.1.1 ∨ ends e ⊆ t.1.2
  (∀ S ⊆ E, 2 ≤ S.card →
    (∀ e ∈ S, ∀ f ∈ S, e ≠ f → Disjoint (ends e) (ends f)) →
    (soft.filter (fun t => t.2 && decide (lists S t))).length =
      (soft.filter (fun t => !t.2 && decide (lists S t))).length) →
  let Fn := (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool
  let obs := fun (f : Fn) (R T : Finset (Fin n)) =>
    f (fun i => decide (i ∈ R)) (fun j => decide (j ∈ T))
  let valid := fun f : Fn => (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size+1 ≤ 2*n ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun i j : Fin n => decide (i=j)) C ∧
    ∀ x y, f x y = C.eval (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)) ∧
    ∀ z ∈ hard, obs f z.1 z.2 = false
  let code := fun f : Fn => (pairs n).map (fun e => obs f (ends e) ∅)
  let size := fun f : Fn => ((code f).filter id).length
  let score := fun f : Fn => (soft.filter (fun t => decide (obs f t.1.1 t.1.2 = t.2))).length
  let bank := fun B : Finset (Fin n) => (List.finRange n).map (fun i => decide (i ∈ B))
  let input := header n ++ header hard.length ++ hard.flatMap (fun z => bank z.1 ++ bank z.2) ++
    header m ++ soft.flatMap (fun t => bank t.1.1 ++ bank t.1.2 ++ [t.2])
  ∃ (k : Nat) (G R : Fin k → Fin k → Bool), write input = paint k G R ∧
    let out := fun P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) => decode (input ++
      (List.finRange k).flatMap (fun i => bits (k.log2+1) (P i).val))
    let red := fun P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) => ((pairs k).filter
      (fun e => decide (P e.1 = e.2) && R e.1 e.2)).length
    (∀ P, perfect k G P → ∃ f : Fn, valid f ∧ out P = code f ∧ red P = (m+1)*size f+score f) ∧
    (∀ f : Fn, valid f → ∃! P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k), perfect k G P ∧ out P = code f) ∧
    ∀ s j : Nat, s ≤ n/2 → j ≤ m →
      Nat.card {P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) // perfect k G P ∧ red P = (m+1)*s+j} =
        Nat.card {f : Fn // valid f ∧ size f = s ∧ score f = j}) ∧
  ∀ (h : Nat) (G R : Fin (2*h) → Fin (2*h) → Bool),
    let v := 2*h
    let n := v+2
    let oldEdges := ((pairs v).filter (fun e => G e.1 e.2)).map (fun e => (e.1.val,e.2.val))
    let reds := ((pairs v).filter (fun e => G e.1 e.2 && R e.1 e.2)).map (fun e => (e.1.val,e.2.val))
    let bans := (pairs n).filter (fun e => decide ((e.1.val,e.2.val) ∉ (v,v+1)::oldEdges))
    let probes := (pairs n).filter (fun e => decide ((e.1.val,e.2.val) ∈ reds))
    let row := fun (e : Fin n × Fin n) => (List.finRange n).map
      (fun i => decide (i = e.1 ∨ i = e.2))
    let zero := List.replicate n false
    reverseQ (paint v G R) = header n ++ header bans.length ++
      bans.flatMap (fun e => row e ++ zero) ++ header probes.length ++
      probes.flatMap (fun e => row e ++ zero ++ [true]) ∧
    let Fn := (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool
    let hit := fun (f : Fn) (e : Fin n × Fin n) =>
      f (fun i => decide (i = e.1 ∨ i = e.2)) (fun _ => false)
    let ok := fun f : Fn => (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size+1 ≤ 2*n ∧
      PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun i j : Fin n => decide (i=j)) C ∧
      ∀ x y, f x y = C.eval (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)) ∧
      (∀ e ∈ bans, hit f e = false) ∧ ((pairs n).filter (hit f)).length = h+1
    ∀ j : Nat, Nat.card {P : Equiv.Perm (Fin v) // perfect v G P ∧
      ((pairs v).filter (fun e => decide (P e.1 = e.2) && R e.1 e.2)).length = j} =
      Nat.card {f : Fn // ok f ∧ (probes.filter (hit f)).length = j}

let header := fun j : Nat => List.replicate j true ++ [false]
let bits := fun (w z : Nat) => (List.range w).map (fun h => z.testBit h)
let pairs := fun k : Nat => (List.finRange k).flatMap (fun i =>
    ((List.finRange k).filter (fun j => decide (i < j))).map (fun j => (i,j)))
∃ (M : Turing.TM2ComputableAux Bool Bool) (c : Nat), (∀ i, Finite (M.tm.Γ i)) ∧
∀ (n : Nat), 2 ≤ n →
  ∀ (hard : List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)))
    (soft : List ((Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)) × Bool)),
  let m := soft.length
  let ends := fun e : Fin n × Fin n => ({e.1,e.2} : Finset (Fin n))
  let E := (pairs n).toFinset.filter (fun e =>
    ∀ z ∈ hard, ¬(ends e ⊆ z.1) ∧ ¬(ends e ⊆ z.2))
  let lists := fun (S : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) (t : (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)) × Bool) =>
    Disjoint t.1.1 t.1.2 ∧ ∀ e ∈ S, ends e ⊆ t.1.1 ∨ ends e ⊆ t.1.2
  (∀ S ⊆ E, 2 ≤ S.card →
    (∀ e ∈ S, ∀ f ∈ S, e ≠ f → Disjoint (ends e) (ends f)) →
    (soft.filter (fun t => t.2 && decide (lists S t))).length =
      (soft.filter (fun t => !t.2 && decide (lists S t))).length) →
  let Fn := (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool
  let obs := fun (f : Fn) (R T : Finset (Fin n)) =>
    f (fun i => decide (i ∈ R)) (fun j => decide (j ∈ T))
  let valid := fun f : Fn => (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size+1 ≤ 2*n ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun i j : Fin n => decide (i=j)) C ∧
    ∀ x y, f x y = C.eval (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)) ∧
    ∀ z ∈ hard, obs f z.1 z.2 = false
  let code := fun f : Fn => (pairs n).map (fun e => obs f (ends e) ∅)
  let size := fun f : Fn => ((code f).filter id).length
  let score := fun f : Fn => (soft.filter (fun t => decide (obs f t.1.1 t.1.2 = t.2))).length
  let bank := fun B : Finset (Fin n) => (List.finRange n).map (fun i => decide (i ∈ B))
  let input := header n ++ header hard.length ++ hard.flatMap (fun z => bank z.1 ++ bank z.2) ++
    header m ++ soft.flatMap (fun t => bank t.1.1 ++ bank t.1.2 ++ [t.2])
  ∀ k : Nat, 1 ≤ k →
    let x := header k ++ input
    let count := fun s j : Nat => Nat.card {f : Fn // valid f ∧ size f = s ∧ score f = j}
    let output := (List.range (n/2+1)).flatMap (fun s =>
      (List.range (m+1)).flatMap (fun j => bits k (count s j % 2^k)))
    Nonempty (Turing.TM2OutputsInTime M.tm (x.map M.inputAlphabet.invFun)
      (some (output.map M.outputAlphabet.invFun)) ((x.length+2)^(c*(k+1))))
changed.unlocks: Computes every count modulo a specified power of two with an explicit uniform time bound. Multiple and imperfect agreements are included.
changed.context: Give red edges weight X and blue edges weight one. The coefficient of X^((m+1)s+j) in the symmetric adjacency hafnian counts the fitting functions in that bin exactly. Compute every coefficient modulo 2^k directly by Hirai and Namba, preprint Theorem 2.1. Its recurrence has polynomial branching per unit of k, giving time L^(C(k+1)) with unary k. Deal with contradictory negatives by emitting zeros. Output k low bits per bin.
